sense.text:
Before the meat and potatoes, this is why we are here, why we take notes, why we must keep studying, praying, fasting and applying what the Lord told us in the scriptures. Without that, what are we doing?

“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning.” The scriptures, Old Testament to New, are written for us to learn from: to go back and see what we need to do to fix situations, and how we are to deal with each other. How many times do we have to go into the Bible to show our people a mistake somebody else already made, that they made too, never knowing it was in there?

This historical book, this book of advice, of laws, statutes and commandments, tells you exactly what you need to do. It warns you so you don't make those mistakes, and it tells you what is going to happen to those who don't give a damn and keep making the same mistakes. The Bible is the most important book on the planet. You better act like it.

Jude 1:16 is speaking of murmuring, busybodies, gossiping: folks that just can't mind their own damn business. There is so much peace in not knowing things that don't pertain to you, so much tranquility in not knowing all the messed up stuff in people's lives. But no, you want to know everything with your nosy ass. That is why the class starts way back here.

“For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men”: the judgment when he returns. You will not be able to say you didn't know your behavior was wrong. When you keep doing it after we go over this, you deserve whatever happens afterwards.

The ones in the midst of murmuring, gossiping, complaining, being busybodies and talebearing never come to the understanding during a class like this that it is about them. They sit wondering who Deacon is talking about, what happened, what set him off, and they are going to find out. Completely missing the point. A lot of us want to know things that are not for us to know. You are not in administration or leadership, you are not dealing with it, you are not fixing nothing. What you need to know for? You just want to be in the know.

“The invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen”: you see these things plain as day. Anybody who doesn't believe in God is an idiot, however smart they are thought to be, Neil deGrasse Tyson included. If you have not come to the conclusion that we were created and need to do what the Creator told us to do, you are far behind. “So that they are without excuse.”

“When they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations.” In their imaginations they started to do whatever they wanted. That is what people do: forget the book, I'mma do it my way. The Lord said forsake not the assembling of yourselves together, and to wear out the steps of the elders, and they say, I'mma do it my way.

“Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools”: you think you know something, you think you're smart, you think your way is the better way.

They “changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man”, and started to worship other things: themselves, some made-up god, mother nature, science. You gave the credit of creation to a molten image. “Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves”: that is why folks are bugging and tripping. They “worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator”, the things created more than the one that made them. How dumb is that?

This is the type of people we are dealing with: idol worshipers, people in their own imaginations, and these same type of people be gay. Homosexuals. They have their own way of doing things. “Men with men working that which is unseemly”: the Bible calls it unseemly, and you call it love, love is love, in your own imagination. “And receiving in themselves that recompence of their error which was meet”: that is why they have those problems and those issues.

“God gave them over to a reprobate mind.” Reprobates: the person who can't get right. They are seared with a hot iron, they think they know it all, they can't change. And we are talking about people sitting up in here.

Now the particular things these folks do, all of it together: fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness, envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity, and then “whisperers.” A whisperer is murmuring and gossiping behind the scenes, with certain individuals you call your friends, the brother or sister you are close to.

“Backbiters, haters of God.” You mean to tell me the backbiters are in the same category with men with men, women with women, murderers, covetousness and fornication? You are the equivalent of a hater of God, all because you can't control your mouth.

“That they which commit such things are worthy of death.” Worthy of death, for whispering and backbiting. It is a character flaw, and the ones who most need to hear it are not even focused on it. You know the individuals in the congregation that can't keep their mouths closed, always complaining, always gossiping, always involved in some mess, because they can't control their mouth.

“These are murmurers, complainers, walking after their own lusts.” These are the type: they complain, they murmur, they walk after their own lusts. They think they are God's greatest gift on earth, that things should be done the way they think, that protocols should be what they think they should be.

Any system can come under criticism. Any program, any structure, any order set: anybody can sit back and say that shouldn't be done like this, it should be like this, this is stupid. So ask yourself, what type of person are you really?
We were warned: “This know also, that in the last days perilous times shall come.”
“Covetous, boasters, proud.” That prideful spirit won't allow you to take any correction, won't allow you to accept what is being said, and will have you thinking it is everybody but you.

“False accusers”: how many run their mouths and gossip without understanding, without the full knowledge of what is going on, yet have so many opinions about what so-and-so is doing and shouldn't be doing.

“Despisers of those that are good.” Some people just hate that you are doing what you are supposed to do: that you are above them in rank, that you have more time to put in for the truth, that you are active in the body doing things they can't do. So they hate everything you put out and have a problem with every order you give. Every time you turn around they have a suggestion. Nobody asked you. And you don't say it to them; you tell everybody underneath them, all your peers. These are the ones you never know for exhorting anybody, only for bringing problems about everything they see. If they ever did exhort, it would be strange.

precepts.why:
“Blame not before thou hast examined the truth.” You cannot accuse, you cannot blame, until you have seen all that needs to be seen concerning a matter. You look foolish doing it without understanding what is going on.

If your opinion lacks understanding, lacks the pertinent information that explains what is going on, and you still feel it necessary to give it, something is wrong with you. You have been put in many situations that showed you that you jumped the gun, that you didn't know what was going on, and still you feel your opinion matters. It don't.

“Understand first, and then rebuke.” That is the answer to the false accuser.

sense.text:
This is the law. “Thou shalt not go up and down as a talebearer”: going up and down telling people's business. You got the inside scoop, the tea. How is it you know everything that is going on all the time? What are you, the black chronicle? How does all information filter through you, so that some folks know before leadership knows? Talebearer. Some of y'all talk too much.

These are the laws of God, what God said not to do, and it says “among thy people”: that is who we are among. We are not supposed to do this amongst us.

“Neither shalt thou stand against the blood of thy neighbour”: wanting to see your neighbour hurt, bearing false witness. Under the law, if a man was to be stoned, you would be in his blood; if you bore false witness to have your neighbour killed, the Lord told you not to do that.

“Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart.” It is a kind of hatred to be a gossiper, a talebearer, a busybody. You are the reason things keep happening, why people's reputations keep getting scarred, why people are continually at odds with one another. You are the fuel behind it, because you can't shut up. You keep it going.

precepts.why:
“I will behave myself wisely in a perfect way”: that means applying the laws of God, reading what is written and doing what it says. The law is the apple of your eye; this is how you conduct yourself, how you treat your neighbour and your brother. “I will set no wicked thing before mine eyes”: this man has his mind right, a prudent man looking well to his going. “I hate the work of them that turn aside”, turn aside from the laws of God, the way of the Most High. “I will not know a wicked person”: I am not going to put myself around wicked people.

“Whoso privily slandereth his neighbour, him will I cut off.” You privately have some slick, ill things to say about your neighbour: get the hell away from me. “He that walketh in a perfect way, he shall serve me”, but the one privily slandering his neighbour, what does that make him? Ask yourself why you have to do it privately.

“He that telleth lies shall not tarry in my sight.” When you don't know what you are talking about and don't have the whole story, yet you tell it like you know, and it isn't true, that is a lie. You thought you were exempt. Whether you believe it or not, it is a lie.

“That I may cut off all wicked doers from the city of the Lord.” A sensible Israelite in Christ reads that and hides himself from the evil: I don't want my name in the hat with the gossipers and murmurers, I'm moving far from anybody like that. Until your friend gets caught up in murmuring, and now people look at you: that's his boy, he must have been talking to him. We have to get this murmuring spirit far away from us. It is not productive to the body, it doesn't make you stronger in spirit, it won't take you to the next level. So why do it?

sense.text:
“Neither murmur ye, as some of them also murmured, and were destroyed of the destroyer.” Write these examples down, so you can jog your memory when you get the feeling you want to complain, when you have a problem with something that has been set up.

Complainers need listeners, not problem-solvers. And the one who sits and listens to the murmuring and says nothing is no better: complicit, part of the problem. All complainers need an ear, and that is you. Folks complain with no idea how to fix it or make it better; they just feel good saying how jacked up it is. Where does that get us? It doesn't. So stop.

These folks that are complainers have far deeper issues than you could imagine; there is a reason they are so worried about what somebody else is doing. They are not going to murmur to the captains. They come to the ones in the back, the ones not particularly involved in anything, or they search out those familiar spirits. If you have that spirit of gossiping, of needing to be in the know and all in somebody else's business, Satan is going to find you, and you will be named amongst the murmurers and complainers. You are the front line against this evil; without you doing it, it is only going to grow.

When a complainer is met with the solution, you find out real quick they don't want the solution. They feel good talking about it, venting, going through everything that occurred. Let's not talk about the problem, let's talk about how we are going to fix it, and hold them to that solution: you think so-and-so did it? Go talk to them, and I'm going to ask them if you did. Take everything away from them, and now they have to deal with their problems. Complainers don't want to deal with the problem. Often they do it to empower themselves, to make the brothers and sisters believe they have the answers and should be sought out by leadership for counsel. No: everything is to be done decently and in order. Don't empower these folks.

Some want to dump all their problems on you, as though you were a trash bin: minutes, hours, days, some for a lifetime. Stay the hell away from me; I am not your recycling bin. I'll help you fix it and we'll be done. Some people are good at sitting with a person and talking it through, and if you are one who just needs to talk it out, locate individuals like that. That is different from a murmurer. We all had better deal with murmuring swiftly and shut it down. Don't let somebody come to you complaining about an officer or a sister when they are not ready to deal with that officer or that sister. You have told me; now you have 24 hours to go tell so-and-so how you feel. Imagine if every person a murmurer went to said, nope, stop: that murmurer would be fixed immediately, because they would know they can't do it here.

It be like that: a week before, brothers are asking every question they can about Deuteronomy 28 and how to break it down, but the moment judgment is given and they are told what the scriptures say, all of a sudden, I don't think they know what they're talking about.

precepts.why:
Remember where Israel came from. They were slaves in Egypt under hard bondage, the Egyptians kicking their butts. Out of nowhere the Most High brought Moses to deliver them. They saw the water turned to blood throughout the land, the plagues fall on the Egyptians and not on them, the power of God showing all the Egyptian gods to be nothing. God killed the firstborn of every house without the blood on the posts. They walked out with the gold and jewelry of the Egyptians that beat them. The Lord split the Red Sea, they walked between two waters to safety, and the Egyptians were swallowed up behind them.

Then “they went three days in the wilderness, and found no water”, and after all that power they got their ignorant asses to the wilderness talking about I'm thirsty, as though the Lord doesn't know you need something to drink. “And the people murmured against Moses, saying, What shall we drink?”

Yet the Lord showed mercy: “the Lord shewed him a tree, which when he had cast into the waters, the waters were made sweet.” “If thou wilt diligently hearken to the voice of the Lord thy God”, and keep his statutes, “I will put none of these diseases upon thee, which I have brought upon the Egyptians”: brought upon them for you. “For I am the Lord that healeth thee.”

After they murmured, God gave them water. Then “the whole congregation of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness”: “Would to God we had died by the hand of the Lord in the land of Egypt.” The same people who saw the sun removed and darkness on the whole land but their one spot. How does that happen? We are a rebellious people, that is how.

“When we sat by the flesh pots, and when we did eat bread to the full.” Imagine the Lord delivering us out of Babylon, and out in the wilderness somebody wishes he had died because he could eat McDonald's every day in America, Popeyes, Bojangles. Imagine seeing all the powers come to an end and complaining that you wish you had died so you could stay and eat Mickey D's. That is a murmurer; it is in your soul. You're over there complaining about bugs and mosquitoes. You were supposed to die. You weren't supposed to make it; you just made the first cut.

“For ye have brought us forth into this wilderness, to kill this whole assembly with hunger.” Is that what happened? Their imagination told them that. We are a rebellious house, because it is still happening today. You are awake and know who you are after the earth worked so hard to hide your history and heritage, a sign that God is real, and still you complain.

“Your murmurings are not against us, but against the Lord.” Moses gives them the reality: you are complaining about how things are done, and it is not leadership you murmur against, it is God. Protocols are put in place for a reason, and every protocol is for a time, as the Old Covenant was put in place for a time until something else was to come. Got a problem with it? The best and safest thing is to shut up, especially when you know the history of what happens to complainers, murmurers and gossipers.

“I have heard the murmurings of the children of Israel”: he heard all the complaints. Yet “At even ye shall eat flesh, and in the morning ye shall be filled with bread; and ye shall know that I am the Lord your God.” The Lord showed mercy again.

“Give us water that we may drink.” “Why chide ye with me? wherefore do ye tempt the Lord?” Then: “Wherefore is this that thou hast brought us up out of Egypt, to kill us and our children and our cattle with thirst?” The same thing again, knowing good and well that wasn't it. Complainers put out crazy scenarios like that to make you feel a certain type of way, to make you feel bad or get you to do what they want.

“They be almost ready to stone me.” Yet the Lord said, “thou shalt smite the rock, and there shall come water out of it.” The Lord yet again showed mercy.

Even after all the complaining the Lord was still showing mercy, and still “all the children of Israel murmured against Moses and against Aaron”: “Would God that we had died in the land of Egypt! or would God we had died in this wilderness!” Who are they saying this to? To God. “Were it not better for us to return into Egypt?”

“And they said one to another”: check the spirit. “Let us make a captain, and let us return into Egypt.” Those imaginations: set up our own leader and go back to Egypt.

“How long shall I bear with this evil congregation, which murmur against me?” Yes, the Lord runs out of patience too. He was patient when they asked for water and for food, and it wasn't good enough; they complained, complained, complained. And he did not say against Moses or against Aaron: “which they murmur against me.”

“As ye have spoken in mine ears, so will I do to you.” Keep on asking for it then: they said they wished they had died in the wilderness, and “Your carcases shall fall in this wilderness.” Then he gets specific: all that were numbered “from twenty years old and upward, which have murmured against me, Doubtless ye shall not come into the land”, save Caleb and Joshua. “But your little ones, which ye said should be a prey, them will I bring in.”

How did they despise the land when they only wanted water and food? You don't bite the hand that feeds you. The same hand that is going to give you that land, you had better please. If you murmur, complain, talebear, gossip, the Lord said he is going to kill you. You thought it was a game.

“His mercy endureth for ever”: is the Lord not merciful? Yes, and we need it, because we are rebellious as all get out. “Blessed are they that keep judgment, and he that doeth righteousness at all times”: full-time, not only when you are here. Nobody is murmuring right now in class; keep that same energy when nobody is looking, when you are with your best friend, the person you feel comfortable with. That is when it counts.

“Our fathers understood not thy wonders in Egypt; they remembered not the multitude of thy mercies.” They forgot all of it. Is that us now? Have we forgotten how patient the Lord has been with each one of us? He rebuked the Red Sea and it dried up; they walked on dry ground; “there was not one of them left.” “Then believed they his words”, and “They soon forgat his works; they waited not for his counsel”: hasty, I need it now. “He gave them their request; but sent leanness into their soul”: it came with a price.

“They envied Moses also in the camp, and Aaron the saint of the Lord. The earth opened and swallowed up Dathan.” They despised order and structure, murmurers and complainers, and “the flame burned up the wicked.” There was a lesson to learn in the wilderness; have we not learned yet? “Thus they changed their glory into the similitude of an ox that eateth grass”, the same imagination as Romans 1. They forgot the God who did “Wondrous works in the land of Ham”: the Egyptians were Hamites, black folks, the same Nilotes in Africa today.

“Therefore he said that he would destroy them”, for murmuring, complaining, their imaginations and serving other gods, had not Moses stood in the breach. “They believed not his word: But murmured in their tents.” That is where it all happens. Brothers, your wives hear you complaining about leadership, and then you wonder why your wife isn't subject to you. You don't respect order, so why would she? You buck every order you get and wonder why your house is out of order.

“Therefore he lifted up his hand against them, to overthrow them in the wilderness: To overthrow their seed also among the nations, and to scatter them in the lands.” The same God that brought the frogs and locusts and hail and fire together; you are going to complain against a God like that? This should be far from us, because what was written aforetime was written for our learning.

sense.text: People who murmur and complain don't think of themselves as furious people, but a liar, a murmurer, all fit in that same category when rolling in that spirit. “Make no friendship with an angry man; and with a furious man thou shalt not go”: don't be around these people. “Lest thou learn his ways”, because emotions transfer, and that spirit transfers. Just as Romans 15:4 said, whatever is written is written for our learning. Stay away from these people and from that spirit.

“A talebearer revealeth secrets”: talking about everybody's business. “But he that is of a faithful spirit concealeth the matter.” A faithful spirit tells you the person's character. There are things about people in this room, things brothers have come and talked about, that a faithful man would never tell anybody. What is the benefit in telling it? How does it help that person? Always weigh why you would share the information: what is the need, why do they need to know, and how will it hurt the person you are talking about?

This is the first sign of a talebearer: they come to you with somebody else's affairs. Once you see that flag, move around, and make them feel uncomfortable. It is healthy in the body to make talebearers, murmurers and gossipers feel uncomfortable and out of place, because it helps stop the behavior. Some of y'all look like this: big mouth, big ears. The gossiper needs a listening ear, and some of y'all supply it for your neighbour.

Other signs: they always say, don't tell nobody. The moment they say that, they are about to say something out of order; they already broke someone else's trust. Gossipers can't hold no water.

“He that goeth about as a talebearer revealeth secrets.” They tell your innermost, darkest secrets: the stuff you vented in confidence, thinking nobody would know, but you told the wrong person. Some of y'all know it right now: after you spoke to somebody, you see how they talk to you about everybody else's business, and you know your information isn't confidential. You are just waiting for it to come out.

“Therefore meddle not with him that flattereth with his lips.” They probe you for information. You think they are trying to help you, a counselor, a listening ear; they just want the tea. Some people feel better about their own lives by hearing the messed up things you are going through; they feed off it. You can't go to a talebearer for help.

precepts.why:
The talebearer doesn't understand this rule: “Rehearse not unto another that which is told unto thee, and thou shalt fare never the worse.” It is unheard of to them; they cannot abide by it; they have to say something. There is no reason for it.

“He that can rule his tongue shall live without strife.” This one is not caught up in the nonsense. He sits back and watches: oh, this is why you stay in trouble, why you keep getting stood up in front of the body, why your name is dung in the nation, because you can't keep your mouth shut. He knows there is a time to speak and a time to be quiet.

“And he that hateth babbling shall have less evil.” The babbler just has to talk, rattling off everything going on. Brothers, you told everybody what goes on in your household, everything your wife does wrong and nothing about what is wrong with you, and now brothers look at your wife a certain type of way. The one who hates talking a lot won't run into those problems; those who talk a lot are always caught in the midst, their names constantly brought up.

“Whether it be to friend or foe, talk not of other men’s lives; and if thou canst without offence, reveal them not.” That is the character you are supposed to possess. A talebearer doesn't understand this rule of thumb; in his mind he has to say something.

Read verse 6 once more, “He that can rule his tongue shall live without strife”, and identify yourself. Is this you? Be honest. Do you find yourself on the phone about things going on in this congregation or another, about somebody you never spoke to directly, something you watched happen and said nothing about? If that is you, this is about you. To stop, you have to recognize it, be real with who you are, and stop, or you will keep that ill name.

sense.text:
They fish for information, asking too many personal questions. These folks probe; they have to know all the details. If they could have you make a movie of it, you would make it for them. Why? Because they ain't got nothing else to do.

“But let none of you suffer as a murderer, or as a thief, or as an evildoer, or as a busybody in other men’s matters.” The same energy you have about never being looked at as a murderer, a thief, an evildoer, you must have about being called a busybody: nosy. Nobody likes that title, yet many are doing everything that qualifies them for it. If you take issue with it, make sure you don't possess the behavior of a busybody.

They thrive on drama: they wake up needing it, grow in it, and are made happy by knowing what nobody else knows, like a soap opera. When something is wrong between brothers, they are somehow part of it, the common denominator every time, the TMZ of Israel in the body, wanting to be the first to drop it. And when it is time to deal with the common denominator, they say, what did I do?

They talk about people but never to the actual person. Why does the golden question never get asked: did you talk to him? As a man you should feel uncomfortable speaking about a problem before you have dealt with that person, and sisters the same. A person may go to their counselor first because they wonder if they are out of the spirit, but let that be the basis of the conversation: this is how I see it, this is what happened in my sight, I know they have a whole other story. That shows you are coming from a neutral standpoint and truly want to solve the problem.

“Go and tell him his fault between thee and him alone.” Is that not what Christ told us to do? How many issues would be alleviated if you just followed what Christ said? Boom, it's finished, we handled that. “If he shall hear thee, thou hast gained thy brother.”

“But if he will not hear thee, then take with thee one or two more, that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established.” This is the proper protocol whenever someone has sinned against you. It doesn't say go tell ten people so they can make you feel good about being right. Go to that person and deal with it; you don't need an audience.

You told twenty people, and now, if they are simple, they look at this brother or sister with a side eye. The simple don't understand there is another side; they come up with twenty different conclusions, all because you shared your side and the other person never got to say what was what. It could have been a misunderstanding, but you needed twenty people to cosign you first.

precepts.why:
Those twenty people are part of the problem: when you don't say something, you give fuel to the murmurer and the complainer. Romans 1 named the whisperers, the backbiters, the haters of God, and verse 32 went over a lot of heads. “Who knowing the judgment of God, that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them.”

It isn't just the ones doing the whispering and the backbiting. The ones that don't say nothing, who just listen and never say, oh, did you talk to the person, are the ear to the murmurer and the complainer, and they have pleasure in it. God said they are worthy of death as well. You aren't exempt. That is why you have to say something.

sense.text:
They switch up depending on who is around. They say all types of things with you, and when the person walks in mid-sentence, some stand bold and say it anyway, but some switch up: I really didn't understand it, we should wait to hear what they have to say, hey, I didn't even see you there. I see where you really are. Don't even ask me what time it is.

“Help, Lord; for the godly man ceaseth.” “They speak vanity every one with his neighbour: with flattering lips and with a double heart do they speak.” They are double-tongued, speaking with a double heart. Don't let this be named amongst us.

They can't keep confidential things confidential; they can't hold water. Tell them something and you might as well have said it on the loud speaker. “Whoso discovereth secrets loseth his credit”: instantly, because now everybody knows he is a blabbermouth. “And shall never find friend to his mind”: that is why it is hard for you to make friends. Watch the one who can't control their mouth; they typically have trouble making friends, because they lack self-control.

“Love thy friend, and be faithful unto him”: faithful when he is with you and when he is not. Reveal his secret and “follow no more after him”: you might as well let that person go. To win them back as your friend is damn near impossible.

“For as a man hath destroyed his enemy; so hast thou lost the love of thy neighbor.” “As one that letteth a bird go out of his hand, so hast thou let thy neighbour go”: the moment you open the window or open your hand, the bird is gone. So with the friend whose secrets you ran your mouth about, blabbering on in Israel to everybody, or to one person. “Follow after him no more, for he is too far off.”

“As for a wound, it may be bound up; and after reviling there may be reconcilement”: you can wound your friend by accident and heal. How many fought their friends when they were young, black eye and all, and were cool after? “But he that betrayeth secrets is without hope.” Betray secrets and see what happens; the scripture says let him go.
Go back to it: “or as a busybody in other men’s matters.” Another word for busybody is nosy. That is the best way to put it.

precepts.why:
“And withal they learn to be idle, wandering about from house to house; and not only idle, but tattlers also and busybodies, speaking things which they ought not.” This is spoken of the younger widows, the young women who lost their husbands. These busybodies just have a desire to know.

Brothers, you don't need to know everything. Some have been privileged to sit amongst leadership, in the backyard of a leader's house, and overheard a conversation not said to them. You would be a complete and utter idiot to utter it. When leaders discuss a matter, they are coming to a solution to deal with it; nothing is shared unless the one hearing it has to deal with it. If you are not dealing with it, you don't need the information. The elder sisters and senior sisters counsel and discuss things to help a person; that doesn't open the door for anybody else to talk about sister so-and-so. There is a need-to-know basis.

There is so much peace in not knowing. Before he was a deacon, Israel was so beautiful, everything grand, shalom to everybody, Christ coming back any day now. Then in a seat of leadership you find out about all the problems, the room gets darker, and you learn some of us are just as bad as the people outside these doors; Satan is attacking. It was far better before you knew. Even a deacon over his regions doesn't ask about other regions that have their own deacon; it is none of his business. Stay in the place of not needing to know. Stop being so nosy. Leave it be.

This has always been a problem: “For we hear that there are some which walk among you disorderly, working not at all, but are busybodies.” They are not doing nothing, so they have time to want to know everything. They have no business of their own; they are idle, like the widows wandering from house to house trying to get all the tea, all the info.

sense.text: Another word for it is meddling. “He that passeth by, and meddleth with strife belonging not to him, is like one that taketh a dog by the ears.” Grab a dog by the ears and you are going to get bit. You are over here being nosy, trying to be all in the Kool-Aid, and you will mess around and get bit. What reaction did you think was going to happen? Now you're involved: so-and-so asked me about that too; why is this brother inquiring about this? How about you just mind your damn business. Don't meddle in affairs that don't pertain to you.

precepts.why: “My son, meddle not with many matters: for if thou meddle much, thou shalt not be innocent; and if thou follow after, thou shalt not obtain, neither shalt thou escape by fleeing.” You're in it now. You wanted to know the flavor of the Kool-Aid; now you're making the Kool-Aid, and it is all yours, all because you wanted to be in someone else's business. The scripture says, meddle not.

“It is an honour for a man to cease from strife”: that is what you are supposed to want. “But every fool will be meddling.” Fools meddle, so what does that make a nosy person? Mind your damn business, fool, or you will get caught up in it and be the one to blame.

A whole situation can shift from the people involved to the one who was just being nosy: it's your fault, you're the one running around telling everybody, you're the reason they're at odds, because they have to defend themselves from all the stories being told. Don't let it be named amongst us.

Christ didn't get caught up in that stuff. “Master, speak to my brother, that he divide the inheritance with me.” This man tried to involve Christ in something that had nothing to do with him. “Man, who made me a judge or a divider over you?” Christ didn't want none of that business; it wasn't his and he wasn't meddling with it.

That is how we have to roll in other people's business: it has nothing to do with me, go to them, I'm not trying to get bit and have my name associated with it. We live in a time when the one being talked about may be crazy enough that everybody who knows has to die, and now they come for you. Much of what happens in the streets, people shot one after another over time, is somebody that knows something. It could have been stopped at the door: it ain't none of my business, I ain't meddling. That is the example from Christ.

sense.text: All of these things could be alleviated if we just learn to control our mouths. “Behold, we put bits in the horses’ mouths, that they may obey us; and we turn about their whole body.” A horse is heavy, all that muscle, and you control the whole horse by a little bit in its mouth. That little thing has so much effect over the whole body. That is the tongue.

“Yet are they turned about with a very small helm, whithersoever the governor listeth”: a cruise ship or a warship, steered by a little thing in the water and a little wheel. The same with the tongue.

“Even so the tongue is a little member, and boasteth great things. Behold, how great a matter a little fire kindleth!” Your tongue can mess up a whole lot. It has that much power, so guard it. Be careful what comes out of it, so you don't tarnish your name or ruin your situation or somebody else's.

precepts.why: “A man’s belly shall be satisfied with the fruit of his mouth.” “Death and life are in the power of the tongue: and they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof.” The tongue can get you killed or give life. Be mindful, because your mouth can either get you rewarded or get you into a whole lot of trouble.

“Keep thy tongue from evil, and thy lips from speaking guile.” Ruling over your tongue takes practice, especially for those who don't know they have no control. They think it's normal to murmur, to complain, to talk about everybody else's problems and business; it has been normalized, they watched their mama do it. It is not normal, not right, not how we are supposed to conduct ourselves. “Depart from evil, and do good; seek peace, and pursue it.”

“Whoso keepeth his mouth and his tongue keepeth his soul from troubles. Proud and haughty scorner is his name, who dealeth in proud wrath.” Learn to control your mouth and you keep yourself from troubles. Some have dodged many bullets because they held their tongue or stayed out of something, never knowing the world of hurt they avoided. Get good at holding your tongue and you will never know what the one who can't control his mouth has to go through.

“Be not rash with thy mouth, and let not thine heart be hasty to utter any thing before God: for God is in heaven, and thou upon earth: therefore let thy words be few.” Control your mouth. There is a time and a place for everything. Be mindful of the things you say to people, and the things you take in as well.

“He that keepeth his mouth keepeth his life: but he that openeth wide his lips shall have destruction.” The man with the control to hold his tongue preserves himself.

These are the examples read over and over: the Lord put a whole generation to death because they were murmuring and complaining and couldn't control their mouths. God ain't playing with gossip and talebearing, so we can't play with it either.
